I've been running a trading bot on my TG for a while now and have used @digitalocean and other services to store its trading logs and market data.

As that history grows, I realized that I need to keep a copy separate from the server running the bot, so I don't lose it if I move the bot to another server or rebuild its setup.

I also want to be able to reuse that history if I change tools or try another AI model, rather than starting from scratch.

@WalrusProtocol launched Walrus Console, and what caught my attention was the decentralized storage aspect.

The data is distributed across independent storage operators, so the network is designed to keep stored files accessible even when some operators go offline.

It brings the files, API access, encryption, and access controls into one place, which sounds easier than bouncing between other services (which I've been doing, and it sucks ngl).

I saw that they're currently offering 5GB of free storage, so I created an API key, and I'm going through the process of connecting it to my bot.

I'll let you know how it goes.

Disclosure: I'm a $WAL holder.

Quantum computing might be crypto's biggest threat.

It could one day drain wallets by cracking the keys that protect them.

Ethereum has a 2029 deadline, but Starknet might leave Ethereum to move faster.

Here's where 9 of the biggest names in crypto stand:

1. $ETH: Targeting full quantum resistance by the end of 2029, covering wallets, validators, and the data layer the whole network runs on. 

It's also building a way for existing wallets to switch to quantum-safe signatures on their own schedule, so nobody gets forced to move funds all at once.

2. $BTC: Developers are working on proposals like BIP-360 to cut the risk from quantum attacks.

The harder problem is lost coins. Millions of BTC sit in old wallets whose owners will never come back to upgrade, and deciding what happens to them is gonna be ugly.

3. $NEAR: Already supports quantum-resistant signatures through ML-DSA. 

You can upgrade your wallet's security without changing your address or moving your assets, which is a big deal if you've got money spread across DeFi.

4. $STRK: Wants to be fully quantum-resistant by 2027. Starknet wallets can already switch to new signature types on their own, but upgrading the network itself still means waiting on Ethereum.

That's mainly why the team is considering becoming its own L1. Nothing's decided yet.

5. $QTC: Quantus went the other way. Instead of upgrading an existing chain, it launched in September with quantum-resistant signatures built in from day one, plus Bitcoin-style proof of work and a 21M supply.

The tech is interesting, but it's a very young network that still has to prove it can attract real users.

6. $TRX: TRON has quantum-resistant signatures running on its testnet.

@justinsuntron says they're ready to bring them to mainnet at any time. I'd watch for when regular users can actually use them.

7. $SUI: Just completed its first native quantum-safe transaction on devnet, using a signature system called ML-DSA-65. Mainnet support is targeted for early 2027.

8. $ZEC: Zcash is working toward quantum resistance through its Tachyon roadmap, and it has a harder job than most. It has to protect funds without breaking the privacy features people use it for, so swapping out wallet signatures won't cut it.

9. $COIN: Coinbase could matter just as much. They're working with Bitcoin developers and researchers on how to move existing BTC wallets to quantum-resistant security, and they've said the lost-coins question needs its own debate alongside that work.

So how serious is the quantum threat?

Today's computers can't realistically break the cryptography protecting Bitcoin and Ethereum wallets. 

A future quantum computer might by working backwards from a wallet's public key to its private key and draining the funds.

Nobody knows when that becomes possible. And upgrading billions of dollars of crypto isn't something you do overnight.

I think the most interesting opportunity here could be the infrastructure that helps existing chains upgrade.

• NEAR users can change their security keys without moving their assets.
• Starknet wallets can adopt new signature systems without waiting for a major network upgrade.
• Then there are the teams doing migration work for existing chains, like Coinbase on the Bitcoin side.

Personally, I'd check three things:

1. Is it live? A working mainnet and a roadmap promising 2027 are very different things.
2. Can people upgrade easily? Nobody wants to unwind their DeFi positions just to secure a wallet.
3. Does the token benefit? A chain getting more secure doesn't automatically make its token worth more.

Run the list through the first two and $NEAR is the one name that clearly passes both right now. Everyone else is still on a roadmap or, in QTC's case, too new to be tested.

Which project do you think is best positioned for the quantum era?

i wanted a physical version of my ai agent. Something real in the living room that shows my to-do list and my day, and that my wife can see too.

I bought a seeed reterminal e1002, an e-ink display. e-ink because it looks like paper: no glow, no buzz, it just sits there like a note on the wall (almost)

setup was honestly simple:
- built the open-source muse gadget firmware on my computer with my sdk token in it
- flashed it to the device over usb
- paired it in the muse app (settings, devices, developer mode) thanks @natfriedman 

now every morning at 7am my agent renders my briefing (calendar, top to-dos, weather) and pushes it to the screen. my wife reads it over coffee. it basically became the family's shared to-do list

whole thing took ~20 min. your agent doesn't have to live in a chat window. give it a physical representation!
